newsitem.title: BRAZIL: FOCUS-BellSouth group wins Brazil cellular prize.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-BellSouth group wins Brazil cellular prize.

text.p: A group led by BellSouth Corp of the United States won a lucrative cellular telephone contract covering Sao Paulo city Wednesday with a $2.45 billion bid that staggered rivals and analysts by its size.

The BCP consortium, which also includes Banco Safra, media group O Estado de Sao Paulo and telecommunications equipment manufacturer Splice, all of Brazil, beat six other groups when it offered 2.647 billion reais for the 20-year concession.

The offer was nearly four times the Communications Ministry's asking price of 600 million reais and more than 1.0 billion reais above the second highest bid. Market analysts had expected the winning bid would be about 2.0 billion reais.

Some government officials said they believed the bid to the biggest ever made for a cellular telephone concession. But members of the winning group played down suggestions they might have paid over the odds.

"The Sao Paulo market warrants this kind of investment," said Roberto Peon, Bellsouth Latin America president. "It's one of the biggest investments in the world, but Sao Paulo is one of the most important cities in the world."

The group would invest up to $600 million over the next two years, including purchases of Northern Telecom's Time Division Multiple Access system, and planned to offer 400,000 lines within 12 months, Peon said.

In the longer term, BCP had its sights on a "good percentage" of the 800,000 to one million people believed to be waiting for a cellular telephone access in Sao Paulo, South America's largest city, Peon said.
Analysts noted that while BCP's cash offer for the concession was much higher than those of its rival bidders, its proposed rates were also far more expensive.

"We expected the winning bid to come in at about two billion reais," said Alexandre Gartner, a telecommunications analyst with Rio investment bank Bozano, Simonsen. "But the group must have done its sums. Those tariffs are way higher than the rest."
A basket of cellular rates included in the BCP bid stood at 82.42 reais, only two reais cheaper than those of Telesp , a local subsidiary of Telebras which currently enjoys a monopoly in Sao Paulo.
Some bidders for the Sao Paulo concession offered rate baskets as low as 59.74 reais.
But BellSouth's Peon said he did not believe the high rates would discourage Sao Paulo residents from becoming BCP customers.

"Paulistas are inseparable from cellphones, not like Americans who leave their phones in their cars," he said. "There are cultural reasons for the Latin American's love of cellphones. We prefer to be communicating all the time."
BellSouth and Banco Safra, who are already partners in an Israeli cellphone venture, each have a 48 percent share in BCP. The rest is divided between O Estado de Sao Paulo and Splice.
The Sao Paulo city concession forms part of the Brazilian government's plan to tender out ten regional cellphone contracts on a private sector-only B Band frequency.
Another, smaller concession to provide B Band services in the northeastern states of Bahia and Sergipe was awarded Wednesday to a group led by Italy's state-owned telecom giant Stet.

The group, which also includes Bradesco bank, the Globopar investment wing of the Globo media empire and textile group Vicunha, bid 250 million reais for the concession, 20 million reais above the government's asking price.
